remainingBlockingDefects.problem: The Greek letters κ and τ in caption 2 come out in a bold/italic DejaVu Serif face that reads as a capital K and a capital T. At 1080p in the English line it looks like 'Curvature K and torsion T'. Chapter 3 uses K for Gaussian curvature, so the film's first script line teaches a wrong or confusing symbol. In the Chinese line the κ also looks like an italic K.
remainingBlockingDefects.fix: Change the GR() helper. Drop font-weight inheritance (set font-weight:400 explicitly; the caption's weight 600 and the English weight 500 are leaking in). Use a face with a distinctive lowercase κ, such as Cormorant Garamond italic or Noto Serif italic. Make font-size 1.15-1.2em. In the English line use a lighter colour or a small letter-spacing so κ/τ do not read as K/T. Check at 1080p that κ has the open, detached arms of a lowercase kappa.

authorKnownIssues: shot.mjs reports 14-25 ms per steady-state frame at 960x540 and 250-600 ms on frames that first compile shaders or KaTeX. It may not include the full GPU time, so real software-GL cost could be higher.

qa.mjs flags the hero frame at t=6.0 as a luminance jump (mean luma ~20 -> ~105) and motion spike. This is the intended hit, and it lasts about 2 frames. Its peak has a slightly grey veil from bloom and flash, which I reduced but did not remove.
The osculating circle occasionally passes behind the HUD readout and the caption. The rings and floor grid can cross the caption.
The kit.chapterTitle 'spread' reveal makes the first glyph look striped for a few frames, and the mono HUD at the left is small (21-30 px) but legible at 1080p.
The gold hero ring plus a cyan ring sweep across the title area at 6.1-6.9 with slight CA fringing. Repeated renders differ by up to 2/765 in the UI text region only (font raster noise).
The echo curves are faint and read mostly as thin arcs. The polar-grid floor is fairly prominent, which reduces negative space in the middle frames.
The scene ends with the knot centred, not carrying the right-shift used under the title. That is intended for the zoom transition into chapter 02.
engineRequests: Optional: expose a frame or seed index to ctx so grain and UI text raster can be bit-identical between renders.
kit.arrow allocates new geometry on every set() call and never disposes the old buffers. A dynamic-buffer variant would be safer for long renders.
